title: Less-than loop from its two cases
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a register state whose fifteen values are at most $B$. If the random-index value of $\sigma$ is less than its vertex-count value, assume that for every $a\le B$ the program started at the index routine for the walk site, with the row counter set to $a$ and all other values as in $\sigma$, has all live register values at most $B$, terminates along every sequence of choices, and has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability $1-q$ for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts. If the vertex-count value is at most the random-index value, assume the same property for every $a\le B$ when started at the continuation label with the row counter set to $a$. Then the program started at the less-than loop label from $\sigma$ has those bounded-register termination and probability properties.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a register state bounded by $B$
if random index is less than vertex count, every row-counter update bounded by $B$ gives the stated property at the walk-site index routine
if vertex count is at most the random index, every row-counter update bounded by $B$ gives the stated property at the continuation label
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a
record of 15 natural-number register values, with every register at most $B$. If
$\sigma$'s random index is less than its vertex count, assume that for every $a\le B$
the program satisfies the specified bounded-register termination and
acceptance-probability property with probability $q$, starting at the index routine for
the walk site and with the row counter set to $a$. If the vertex count is at most the
random index, assume that for every $a\le B$ the same property holds starting at the
continuation label with the row counter set to $a$. Then the program satisfies that
property with probability $q$ starting at the less-than loop label with initial register
record $\sigma$.
